summary: Volition's Mars-set shooter series built around Geo-Mod destruction, including the open-world Guerrilla and its later Re-Mars-tered edition.

entries.title: Red Faction

emulation.emulator: Native Windows or PCSX2 for PS2 comparison
emulation.notes: Use Windows for the main run; emulate PS2/N-Gage/mobile only for platform-preservation comparison.

primary.why: Red Faction released for PlayStation 2, Windows, Mac platforms, N-Gage, mobile phone, and later PlayStation 4. The Windows version has the highest practical fidelity and includes PC-specific multiplayer/content notes such as the Glass House Geo-Mod sandbox level.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version natively or through a modern PC storefront where available; use PS4 only as a convenient console re-release route and PS2/N-Gage/mobile for preservation comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: The PS4 release is a PS2 re-release with added platform features, not a full remaster.

entries.title: Red Faction II

emulation.emulator: Native Windows or Dolphin/PCSX2/xemu for console comparison
emulation.notes: Use Windows for play; use console emulation only for original-platform comparison.

primary.why: Red Faction II released first on PlayStation 2, then GameCube, Windows, and Xbox. Windows is the highest-fidelity route despite the PC port's mixed reception.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version natively with compatibility fixes if needed; use console versions if you specifically prefer original split-screen console play.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster is documented in the cited public source.

entries.title: Red Faction: Guerrilla
entries.definitive_edition: Red Faction: Guerrilla Re-Mars-tered on Windows

emulation.notes: Use Re-Mars-tered on PC rather than emulating PS3/Xbox 360.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Windows Re-Mars-tered at highest stable settings

primary.why: Guerrilla released on PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and Windows in 2009, then as Re-Mars-tered on Windows, PS4, Xbox One, and Switch. Re-Mars-tered includes the original DLC and technical improvements, and Windows is the highest-fidelity route.
primary.how_to_play: Play Red Faction: Guerrilla Re-Mars-tered on Windows at the highest stable settings; use PS4 Pro/Xbox One X for strong 4K/60fps-capable console routes or Switch for portable play.

entries.remaster_caveats: Re-Mars-tered improves presentation and includes DLC, but cutscenes remain older pre-rendered material.

entries.title: Red Faction: Battlegrounds
entries.definitive_edition: Xbox 360/XBLA version selected as primary route

emulation.emulator: Xenia or RPCS3 where legal and stable
emulation.notes: Use original digital ownership where possible; emulation is preservation-only.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Seventh-generation downloadable console release, potentially improved through emulator scaling

primary.why: Red Faction: Battlegrounds released as a downloadable vehicle combat spin-off on PlayStation Network and Xbox Live Arcade in 2011. With no sourced content split, Xbox 360 is the practical primary route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360/XBLA version if already owned; use PS3/PSN as an equivalent alternate route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Availability depends on legacy digital ownership; no modern remaster is documented in the cited public source.

entries.title: Red Faction: Armageddon
entries.definitive_edition: Windows PC version with Path to War DLC where owned

emulation.notes: Use Windows rather than emulating PS3/Xbox 360.

primary.version: PC version with Path to War DLC where owned
primary.why: Red Faction: Armageddon released for Windows, PlayStation 3, and Xbox 360 in 2011. Windows is the highest-fidelity route, and the Path to War downloadable expansion is the notable content add-on to include where available.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows version natively with the Path to War DLC installed if owned; use console versions only for original-platform comparison.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster is documented in the cited public source; the series stalled after Armageddon's sales disappointment.
